e7_s4_rationale: The presence of a firm, nonpulsatile mass with internal septations and a density similar to subcutaneous fat, as well as the location in the medial thigh and the patient's age, are consistent with fibrolipomatous hamartoma, a benign tumor that typically presents in the thigh of young children.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Lipoma
e7_s4_rejected.why: While lipomas can present as fatty masses, the presence of internal septations and the specific location in the thigh are more suggestive of fibrolipomatous hamartoma.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Liposarcoma
e7_s4_rejected.why: Liposarcomas are malignant tumors that are rare in children and would be expected to show more aggressive features, such as invasion of surrounding tissues or lymphadenopathy, which are not present in this case.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Pleomorphic lipoma
e7_s4_rejected.why: Pleomorphic lipomas are rare and typically occur in older adults, making them an unlikely diagnosis for an 18-month-old child.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Atypical lipomatous tumor
e7_s4_rejected.why: Atypical lipomatous tumors are malignant and would be expected to show more aggressive features, such as invasion of surrounding tissues or lymphadenopathy, which are not present in this case.
